purpose: User review before any further 3D modeling for this city art revision

records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create an ORIGINAL pre-modeling art-direction approval sheet for Bellwake, a bright nostalgic Japanese-anime fantasy RPG town. Input image 1 is ONLY a reference for coherent city planning and broad streets, wall connections and deliberate planting. Input image 2 is ONLY a reference for charming aged building materials, useful architectural details, roof color diversity, sensible broad building proportions. Do not reproduce either screenshot, its labels, logos, UI or advertisements. This output is concept art for human review, NOT a game screenshot or a final sprite atlas.
Art direction: lovingly hand-painted early-2000s Japanese fantasy RPG environment, compact welcoming urban architecture, strong readable dimensional masses, storybook charm with disciplined structural drawing. Soft painted edges and selective crisp highlights, NOT glossy plastic, not CAD, not low-poly toy blocks, not photorealistic PBR. Bright natural daylight from upper left, cool gentle shadows to lower right, warm pale limestone and cream plaster, clear natural greens. No all-over yellow or olive filter. Orthographic oblique view approximately 30 degrees elevation and 45 degrees azimuth; all ground foundations, walls and street directions consistently aligned to the two 2:1 map axes; vertical walls upright. Broad, believable footprints, no skinny stretched high houses.
Roofs are aged handmade ceramic/slate: individual overlapping tile lips, subtle variations in size, placement and value, a few replacement tiles, softly worn ridge caps and slightly imperfect eave silhouette. Orderly construction with organic tile rhythm, NOT mathematically identical clean rows, not balloon/scallop bubble roofs, not holes through the roof. Local oldness: faint rain streaks under gutters, powdery worn plaster revealing small brick patches at the base, rubbed stone thresholds, faded painted shutters, small areas of moss in damp joints. Habitable and well-loved, never derelict. Keep masonry foundations and building placement straight. Restrained baskets, stacked firewood, shop signs, window boxes and vines with visible purpose; don't bury everything in ivy. Strong differences of silhouette and function, not one template recolored.
Deliver a polished spacious LANDSCAPE concept sheet, 3 columns by 2 rows, six SEPARATE standalone building illustrations, comfortably separated on a flat pale warm-grey background. Each building fully visible with its own small foundation only; NO unified city, no connected megablock, no streets joining the six. No decorative card borders or paragraphs. Small discreet labels A, B, C, D, E, F are sufficient. Consistent world scale, don't enlarge a small home to the civic building's size. A tiny simple 3.5-head-tall anime adventurer beside a door in each panel provides the same scale reference.
A top left: compact broad two-storey bakery, warm TERRACOTTA orange-red tiled roof with charcoal replacement tiles, cream and exposed timber shopfront, striped faded cream/russet awning, bread display and hanging loaf emblem, softly rounded three-step entrance facing lower-left map direction. Facade wide enough for a door plus two generous shop windows.
B top middle: grey-SAGE green roof apothecary, L-shaped massing and a modest side stair up to a covered landing, dusky plum shutters, glazed herb bottles, a few flowering plants, entrance facing lower-right. Roof has a small patched strip of lighter old green tiles.
C top right: comfortable two-storey inn, muted PLUM/MAUVE slate roof, long timber balcony and a lower side wing, offset gable, faded moss-green shutters, warm lanterns, sleeping-moon sign; frontage along a map axis, broad rather than towerlike.
D bottom left: low wide smithy, weathered BLUE-GREY slate roof, thick light-stone lower walls, tall working chimney with soot ONLY near its cap, open forge bay, anvil and neatly stacked firewood, wide double service door; the roof silhouette substantially different from the homes.
E bottom middle: humble one-storey courtyard residence with a small attic, faded WARM GREY/clay roof, dormer and short lean-to, repaired plaster, timber lintel, low garden fence and restrained flowering window box, no commercial awning; quieter and smaller than the shops.
F bottom right: adventurers' guild as the civic landmark, pale worn limestone, a welcoming broad entrance and open bell/clock tower, deep muted blue roof accents mixed with weathered stone, asymmetrical subsidiary roof volumes, two tasteful banners; the only significantly taller building, friendly heroic anime-fantasy character, not an enormous cathedral.
Use the varied roof palette exactly in the six intended families. Prioritize charm, lived-in structure and a cohesive paint style over microscopic texture.

Study 1 upper left: a substantial LIGHT warm-grey limestone gatehouse with one deep open arch, thick connected curtain-wall sections extending a short distance along both sides on the same axis. Solid foundations, individual slightly chipped blocks and recessed joints, a real parapet wall-walk, raised iron portcullis, faded blue-and-cream banner. A short pale stone bridge/threshold directly meets the arch; show a small anime traveler through the opening for scale. Wall stone must remain bright, weighty and gently weathered, NEVER charcoal, blackened or green-black.
Study 2 upper right: a separate corner module with a rounded bastion and two orthogonal connected wall runs, seen in 2:1 oblique view. Clear buttressed base, real thick parapets and coping, small arrow recesses, slight dusty deposits at the foot and faint runoff under capstones. Architectural joints join precisely. This is a modular corner sample, not a whole castle.
Study 3 lower left: a separated lineup of FIVE distinct vegetation assets at consistent scale: an older asymmetric broadleaf street tree with several large readable crown groups, visible trunk and small crown gaps; a lighter silver-green birch with airy upper branches; a narrower layered blue-green conifer; a short fruit/courtyard tree with lower branching and dusty green leaves; a young street tree with a smaller irregular crown. Also two small clustered shrubs. Roots grounded, foliage hand-painted with light upper-left and shaded lower-right, NO identical spherical pom-poms, no geometric cones, no neon/olive green, no noise made of thousands of specks. Keep silhouettes distinct and readable.
Study 4 lower right: a small infrastructure-only street-corner kit demonstration: a WIDE muted grey-blue herringbone-paved roadway with small human-scaled bricks, generous pale irregular-stone sidewalk, real low raised curbs with top and side visible. One curving planted corner and one chamfered edge, a lowered accessible entrance ramp, a drainage grate, one elegant slender lamp, one worn wooden bench beside a small brick planter. Curve, lawn and sidewalk share exactly the same outline. A traveler crossing shows the road is several people wide. Keep furnishings at the edges and the walking route open. No houses in this panel.
Bright natural grass, pale weathered masonry and muted paving form one harmonious palette, allowing the roof colors on a separate building sheet to be the accents.

approval.scope: Concept A/B visual direction approved; proceed with individual editable Blender models and in-engine integration. Final model art review remains separate.
